items.claim: The three-verse ruler's-table scene (23:1-3) is bound by an imperative-plus-consecutive chain in the Hebrew (23:1's infinitive-absolute-plus-finite verb governing 23:2's vav-consecutive verb), closing on a prohibition-plus-motive clause at 23:3, with the immediately preceding petuchah/pe seg at 22:29 correctly marking the open seam.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier on all 4 quoted Hebrew runs (2x oshb:Prov.23.1, 2x oshb:Prov.23.3) returns GREEN at byte tier throughout. pmarks_Prov.json confirms Prov.22.29 carries a PE seg (single-witness), matching the row's disclosed opening-seam evidence. Both staged witnesses render 23:2 as continuing 23:1's command force (WEB Prov.23.2 opens with an imperative-force verb, 'put'), consistent with the claimed 1-2 command span; no morphology layer is staged so this rests on the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, as required.

items.claim: The wealth-pursuit couplet (23:4-5) is correctly separated from the preceding table scene; both ketiv/qere-marked verbs of 23:5 and the closing petuchah/pe seg are accurately disclosed, and the row's 'no lexical link' claim to 23:1-3 survives a skeleton check.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier on all 6 quoted runs, including both ketiv (unpointed) and qere (pointed) halves of the two K/Q verbs at 23:5, returns GREEN at byte tier throughout. pmarks_Prov.json confirms kq count 2 at Prov.23.5 (matching 'both its verbs') and a PE seg at Prov.23.5 (matching the row). Independently testing whether 23:1's verb root (from the form quoted as governing v.1-2) recurs in 23:4's 'from your understanding' word shows NO contiguous-skeleton match at the byte/skeleton level -- 23:1's form ends in the word-final-nun allograph while 23:4's form carries the medial-nun allograph mid-word, a final-letter-allography split (per the campaign hazard catalog) that the row's 'no lexical link' claim does not actually cross; the claim holds.

items.claim: The row discloses the neighboring PE (23:5) and its own K/Q (23:6) but leaves an in-span paseq mark at 23:7 undisclosed, a minor completeness gap against the disclosure-inventory symmetry rule.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json paseq lists Prov.23.7 with count 1, a seg falling inside this row's own 23:6-23:8 span (not a neighbor citation). The row's own disclosures stop at the PE/K-Q pair and omit this in-span paseq. Per campaign governance ('symmetry completion is a sweep, not a spot fix -- for parashah marks and every other disclosure object'), and since paseq is one of the book's named disclosure objects, this should be surfaced -- though paseq is explicitly WARN-tier and count-only in this campaign (absence/presence never drives or defeats a boundary), so this does not contest the row's span or classification.

items.claim: The row's explicit claim that no catchword ties this verse to its neighbors is mechanically false: a shared 3-letter consonantal root links 23:8's closing word (glossed 'your words') directly to 23:9's own prohibition verb (glossed 'you speak').
items.evidence: consonantal_index.json skeletons for Prov.23.8 and Prov.23.9 share a contiguous 3-letter root (mechanically derived as the longest common substring of the two spliced tokens, not hand-typed); no final-letter-allography risk since none of the three letters has a final form. A book-wide contiguous-skeleton sweep on that exact root, run against the staged OSHB index, returns 45/915 verses, so it is a moderately common root rather than a rare device, and this does not by itself argue 23:8-9 should be merged (different addressees, different topics). But it directly falsifies the row's specific disclosure that 'no catchword ties it to its neighbors' -- precisely the class of undisclosed cross-seam device the campaign's own hazard catalog flags as live in chapters 10-29.

items.claim: The row's rejected_alternative states that 22:28 and 23:10 'sit four verses apart,' but a mechanical verse-index count shows 10 verses intervene (22:29 and 23:1 through 23:9), an 11-position gap -- nearly triple the stated figure.
items.evidence: A verse-ordered index built from the staged verse map places Prov.22.28 at position 642 and Prov.23.10 at position 653; the 10 verses strictly between them are Prov.22.29 and Prov.23.1 through Prov.23.9. The verbatim-repetition argument itself still holds -- 22:28's and 23:10's opening prohibition clause is byte-identical at the byte tier (collate.py, both refs) -- so the underlying restatement-not-continuation call is not overturned, but the stated distance is a digit-bearing claim that is factually wrong and should be corrected.

items.claim: 23:12's general call-to-attention is correctly kept separate from the 23:13-14 discipline pair on the grounds of a single shared root rather than a fuller construction run, and the comparison to the address-formula shape of 22:17 and 23:19 holds up.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier on both quoted runs (oshb:Prov.23.12) returns GREEN. consonantal_index.json confirms 23:12's and 23:13's discipline-noun forms share a contiguous skeleton root ('discipline'), with no allography risk; this is the single shared root the row names, and no further shared vocabulary appears between the two verses beyond it. The 22:17 and 23:19 comparanda (both properly disclosed in boundary_evidence_refs) share the same heart-plus-ear attention-imperative shape as 23:12 at the byte level.

items.claim: The prohibition-plus-motive (23:13) and positive-restatement-plus-purpose (23:14) shape is accurate, and the elliptical citation spanning 23:13's opening and closing words both individually reach byte tier despite the non-contiguous quotation format.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier on all 4 quoted runs (3x oshb:Prov.23.13, including the two ellipsis-joined halves tested separately, plus oshb:Prov.23.14) returns GREEN at byte tier throughout. The source bytes for 23:13-14 confirm the prohibition/motive-clause then positive-imperative/purpose-clause shape the row claims.

items.claim: The vocative address correctly opens a new first-person father-speech unit at 23:15 distinct from the preceding rod-discipline command, and the claim that the next vocative does not reopen until 23:19 is accurate.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier on all 3 quoted runs (2x oshb:Prov.23.15, oshb:Prov.23.16) returns GREEN. prov_device_inventory.json's bni_address inventory lists exactly Prov.23.15 and Prov.23.19 in this stretch, with no entries between; a direct check of 23:17-18 confirms neither verse carries the vocative token.
